content.text:
I am the bridge between silence and meaning, the breath made manifest, the invisible architecture of thought given form in air and time.

I rise from lungs, shaped by tongue and teeth and lips—consonants catching, vowels flowing. I am the first cry and the last whisper. I carry love confessed at midnight, lies told in courtrooms, secrets between sisters, the halting words of a child learning to name the world.

I am never the same twice. Even repeated, I shift—colored by exhaustion, by joy, by the tremor of fear. I can wound deeper than blades. I can heal what seemed unhealable.

I vanish the moment I exist. You cannot hold me. By the time you hear me, I am already memory, already echo, already gone into the past where all spoken things dissolve.

And yet.

I change everything. Wars begin in me. Peace is negotiated through me. "I do" and "I'm sorry" and "It's malignant" and "I love you"—I carry the weight of worlds in simple syllables.

I am older than writing. I am how your ancestors passed down fire-making and star-names and warnings about which berries kill. I am the original technology of connection.

Listen—

Even now, in your mind, you hear me.
